h1:
Kanchanaburi by Nature
Erawan, Sai Yok & Srinakarin Dam in 3 Days
intro: Kanchanaburi is the real deal when it comes to waterfalls: emerald-clear pools at Erawan, deep forest along the Kwai Noi River at Sai Yok, and then a night on a raft house out on the Srinakarin Dam reservoir. This plan fits it all into 3 days and 2 nights as a self-drive trip — day one is a full day at Erawan, day two heads into the Sai Yok area before you settle onto a raft, and the last morning you wake up to mist over the water before driving back. We've checked the real entry fees and opening hours for 2026 at every stop.

blocks.html: There's far more to natural Kanchanaburi than the Bridge over the River Kwai. Give it about three days and a willingness to drive, and you get limestone falls in shades of emerald that climb tier by tier, rainforest along the Kwai Noi River, and a broad reservoir where you can wake up on a raft to morning mist. This plan keeps you riverside in town for one night, then up on a raft house in the Srinakarin Dam area for a second, so you're not driving in and out of town again and again.

blocks.title: Read this before you set off
blocks.html: These nature spots are spread far apart and in different directions. Erawan Falls sits in Si Sawat district, about 65 km from town, while Sai Yok is out along the western highway (Kanchanaburi–Thong Pha Phum). This route suits self-drivers or anyone renting a car far better than public transport. If you're not driving, a good option is to join a one-day Erawan tour, then charter a car for the Sai Yok–dam day.

items: Day 1 — A full day at Erawan Falls, climbing tier by tier up to level 7, swimming with the schools of soro brook carp, then back to a riverside stay in town.
Day 2 — Head west into Sai Yok National Park, walk the suspension bridge over the Kwai Noi River, stop at Sai Yok Noi Waterfall, then move into the Srinakarin Dam area and check in to a raft house.
Day 3 — Wake to mist over the water at the raft, visit the 7-tier Huai Mae Khamin Waterfall inside the dam park, then ease your way back into town.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Erawan Falls, seven tiers of paradise

blocks.html: Erawan Falls is inside Erawan National Park in Si Sawat district, about 65 km from town — roughly an hour and a half if you drive yourself. Set off early, because the falls have 7 tiers and the climb from the bottom to the top covers around 1,500 metres, with the upper tiers closing before the park itself. Entry is 60 THB for Thai adults and 30 THB for children; foreign visitors pay 300 THB for adults and 150 THB for children, plus 30 THB per car. The park is open roughly 07:30–16:00. For questions, call 034-574234.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: A full day at Erawan Falls

items.activity: Leave Kanchanaburi town heading for Si Sawat district
items.note: Fill up on fuel and grab breakfast before you head up. The drive passes mountain views and reservoirs.

items.activity: Arrive at the Erawan National Park gate and pay the entry fee
items.note: If you carry plastic water bottles up, you leave a 20 THB deposit per bottle — bring them back down to get the money returned.

items.activity: Start at tier 1 and work up to tier 2, Wang Macha
items.note: Tiers 1–3 are easy walking. Tier 2 has big soro brook carp — you can sit and dangle your feet in for the fish to nibble, for free.

items.activity: Climb on to tiers 4–5 and shoot the emerald pools
items.note: From tier 4 up the trail gets steep and rocky. Wear grippy rubber shoes and watch your footing.

items.activity: Reach tier 7, Phu Pha Erawan, the top level
items.note: The round trip to the top is about 2 km. Tier 7 usually closes around 15:00 and tiers 5–6 around 15:30, so going up in the morning is easier.

items.activity: Come down to swim at the lower tiers and have lunch
items.note: You can swim until around 16:00. There are food stalls and seating down below — no food or plastic is allowed on the upper tiers.

items.activity: Pack up and drive back into Kanchanaburi town
items.note: Tonight you sleep riverside on the Kwai in town to rest up properly before heading into the forest tomorrow.

items.activity: Check in to a riverside stay and wander the night market / riverfront
items.note: Evenings by the Kwai are cool and pleasant, with plenty of riverside restaurants and cafés.

blocks.title: Tip for your Erawan Falls day
blocks.html: For clear emerald water and fewer people, head to the upper tiers first thing in the morning, then come down to swim at the lower tiers in the afternoon — because the top tier closes before the lower ones. Arrive late and you may not make it up to tier 7 in time.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Sai Yok National Park, then a raft house on Srinakarin Dam

blocks.html: Today you switch directions and take the western route, the Kanchanaburi–Thong Pha Phum highway. Sai Yok Noi Waterfall sits right beside this road, about 56 km from town, while the larger Sai Yok Yai Waterfall is inside Sai Yok National Park, pouring down into the Kwai Noi River by the suspension bridge. Entry to Sai Yok National Park is 60 THB for Thais and 300 THB for foreign visitors. Spend the morning into the afternoon here, then loop into the Srinakarin Dam area to check in to a raft house.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Sai Yok to the dam raft house

items.activity: Check out and leave town heading for the Thong Pha Phum road
items.note: Tonight you're on a raft, so pack ready and bring swim clothes.

items.activity: Stop at Sai Yok Noi Waterfall (roadside at km 56)
items.note: A low tier of falls right by the road, easy to reach on foot. Nearby is Nam Tok railway station, the end of the Death Railway line.

items.activity: Enter Sai Yok National Park and walk the suspension bridge at Sai Yok Yai Waterfall
items.note: Sai Yok Yai (Khao Jone) flows down into the Kwai Noi River — walk the suspension bridge across the river for photos.

items.activity: Lunch inside the park or at a riverside restaurant
items.note: The park has restaurants and rafts; à la carte dishes start around 60–120 THB a plate.

items.activity: Drive into the Srinakarin Dam area and check in to a raft house
items.note: The Srinakarin Dam reservoir is the largest park in the province, with raft houses across many price levels.

items.activity: Swim off the raft, paddle a kayak, watch the sunset
items.note: The reservoir water is calm and swimmable. Wear a life jacket, especially if you're with kids.

items.activity: Have dinner on the raft and sleep to the sound of the water
items.note: Phone signal is patchy in places — bring a power bank and cash.

blocks.title: Straight talk about the raft houses
blocks.html: Raft houses on Srinakarin Dam range from cheap, simple local rafts to air-conditioned resort rafts, and prices vary hugely. Many quote rates that include meals and the boat transfer, so check exactly what's covered and book ahead — especially over long weekends, when they fill up fast.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Huai Mae Khamin Waterfall, then back to town

blocks.html: The best part of sleeping on a raft is waking to mist drifting over the water. The last day is relaxed: stop at Huai Mae Khamin Waterfall in the central part of the Srinakarin Dam park, a 7-tier limestone falls with clear water. These days there's a paved road right up to it, so you no longer need the car-ferry raft you once did. Entry to the waterfall zone is 60 THB for Thai adults and 30 THB for children; foreign visitors pay 300 / 150 THB. Then ease your way back into town.

items.activity: Wake to mist over the water with coffee on the raft
items.note: The prettiest mist tends to come in the cool late-rains-into-winter stretch, November to January.

items.activity: Breakfast on the raft, then pack up and check out
items.note: Confirm the boat transfer times back to shore with the raft house first.

items.activity: Drive to the 7-tier Huai Mae Khamin Waterfall
items.note: A clear-water limestone falls; each tier has a pool to swim in, and you can climb up to see several levels.

items.activity: Swim at your favourite tier and take photos
items.note: The limestone is slipperier than it looks — wear rubber shoes and watch kids around the deeper pools.

items.activity: Start heading back, stopping for lunch along the way
items.note: There are restaurants and reservoir viewpoints on the way back.

items.activity: Arrive in Kanchanaburi town and finish the trip at a riverside café
items.note: If you've still got energy, stop at a souvenir market for thong muan rolls and honey to take home.

blocks.text: Entry fees for the key stops (updated 2026)

items: Erawan National Park (Erawan Falls) — Thais: adult 60 / child 30 THB · foreigners: 300 / 150 THB · car 30 THB · open roughly 07:30–16:00
Sai Yok National Park (Sai Yok Yai Waterfall) — Thais 60 THB · foreigners 300 THB
Sai Yok Noi Waterfall — free entry, roadside on the Kanchanaburi–Thong Pha Phum road at km 56
Huai Mae Khamin Waterfall (Srinakarin Dam park) — Thais: adult 60 / child 30 THB · foreigners: 300 / 150 THB
Plastic water-bottle deposit at Erawan — 20 THB per bottle, refunded when you bring the bottle back down

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Park entry fees and raft prices can change with policy and season. The figures above come from park information and recent reviews — it's worth calling the park or the raft house's page again before you go, especially in the rainy season when some waterfall trails may close for safety.

items.name: Grippy rubber shoes
items.blurb: The limestone at Erawan and Huai Mae Khamin is very slippery. Wear grippy rubber shoes or water shoes — far safer than flat flip-flops.

items.name: Cash
items.blurb: Park fees, raft houses and many shops in the waterfall areas mainly take cash, and signal is patchy in places.

items.name: Swimwear + dry bag
items.blurb: There's a swimming spot every day. Bring a change of swim clothes, a dry bag for your phone, and a life jacket if you're on the raft with kids.

items.name: Book the raft ahead
items.blurb: Srinakarin Dam rafts fill up fast over long weekends — book several weeks ahead and confirm clearly whether meals and the boat transfer are included.

faq.q: Can you visit Erawan Falls and Srinakarin Dam on the same day?
faq.a: You can push it, but it's tiring. Erawan has 7 tiers that take half a day of climbing, while Srinakarin Dam is about sleeping on a raft and visiting Huai Mae Khamin Waterfall. For a relaxed trip, split them across separate days and allow a night on a raft so you get the full atmosphere.

faq.q: How much is entry to Erawan Falls and what are the opening hours?
faq.a: In 2026, Thai adults pay 60 THB and children 30 THB; foreign adults pay 300 THB and children 150 THB, plus 30 THB per car. The park is open roughly 07:30–16:00 and you can swim until around 16:00, but the top tier (tier 7) closes earlier, around 15:00 — so head up to the upper tiers first thing in the morning.

faq.q: Is the climb to tier 7 of Erawan Falls tiring?
faq.a: Tiers 1–3 are easy walking and fine for kids and older travellers, while tiers 4–7 get steep and rocky. The round trip to the top is about 2 km. Wear grippy rubber shoes, carry water, and don't rush — just climb tier by tier.

faq.q: Is sleeping on a raft house at Srinakarin Dam safe, and what should I bring?
faq.a: Most raft houses are safe and provide life jackets. Wear one when swimming, especially with kids. Bring cash, a power bank and mosquito repellent, since phone signal is patchy in places, and book the raft ahead over long weekends.

faq.q: When is the best time for a nature trip in Kanchanaburi?
faq.a: The cool late-rains-into-winter stretch, November to February, is best: cool weather, the waterfalls still have water, and the mornings bring mist over the dam water. In the rainy season (June–October) the falls run full but the rocks are slippery and some trails may close for safety, so check with the park before you go.
